q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of tissue paper and napkins?
title: Tissue paper carbon footprint per kg
short: For a converter, multiply the parent reels by the mill's per-kg figure and add embossing, folding, cutting and packing electricity per kg passed. A tissue mill adds its pulping, Yankee dryer steam and electricity. Drying is usually the largest energy use.

ul: Pulp or recovered paper by weight.
Yankee dryer and hood: steam and gas.
Pulpers, refiners and vacuum pumps on electricity.
Embossing, folding, log saw and wrapping.

p: Report per kg of saleable tissue, and per pack with grammage and ply count.

example.title: Worked example: napkin converter per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 21,300 / 200,000 = 0.106 kg CO2 per kg
Add the parent reels from the mill for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
